summary: Order placement 500s began at 12:12:31Z, ~2 minutes after order-service deployment dep-5101 (v2.14.0, 12:10Z) which 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders', introducing a new MarginCheckValidator and removing legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(). Error rate jumped from ~0.22% to ~18% (14.74% in the 12:10 bucket) and stayed there. All errors are NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 with 'marginProfile is null' on orderType=FNO (derivatives), matching the support tickets. Latency, CPU, memory, db pool and request rate are flat, and there are no errors in downstream deps (pricing-engine, exchange-gateway, market-data-service, ledger-db) and no order-service config change, ruling out resource, capacity, dependency and config causes. Root cause: a null-dereference regression in the newly deployed validation path in order-service v2.14.0.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) introduced a null-dereference regression in MarginCheckValidator for F&O orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v2.14.0 refactor of order validation added a new MarginCheckValidator and removed the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); the new validator dereferences marginProfile (line 88) which is null for some/all F&O (derivatives) orders, throwing NullPointerException that surfaces as HTTP 500. The fault originates in order-service's newly deployed code.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deployed at 12:10:00Z adds MarginCheckValidator and removes legacy margin validation
New validator dereferences null marginProfile at line 88 for orderType=FNO
NPE converts to HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders
No order-service config change and no downstream errors -> fault is in the release, not config/deps

assumptions: All FNO orders reaching the new validator fail because marginProfile is null; failures began with the new pods, not a coincidental data change
No unseen order-service flag/config change exists outside the queried window

ranked_hypotheses.title: Upstream margin-profile data (ledger-db) became null/incomplete, causing the new strict validator to fail
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A data-side change made marginProfile null for FNO accounts, and the stricter new validator turns that into a 500.

causal_chain.claim: New validator does not null-guard it

assumptions: ledger-db data changed at ~12:12Z despite no logged errors there

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation in order-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: CPU, memory, DB pool or request load exhausted capacity causing 500s.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: cpu (~40%), memory (~60%), db_pool_in_use (~14) and request_rate are all flat across onset; latency p99 flat ~150ms; error pattern is a code NPE, not a timeout/pool error (F6, F7).

facts.statement: order-service error_rate rose from ~0.22% (pre-12:10 buckets) to 14.74% in the 12:10 bucket and ~18% thereafter.
dep-5101 (order-service v2.14.0) deployed at 12:10:00Z added MarginCheckValidator and removed legacy OrderRules.validateMargin().
First NPE occurred 12:12:31Z, ~2 min after the rollout-complete log at 12:10:08Z.
All logged errors are MarginCheckValidator NPEs with 'marginProfile is null' for orderType=FNO.
Latency (p99 ~150ms), CPU (~40%), memory (~60%), db_pool_in_use (~14) and request_rate (~230/s) were flat across onset.
No order-service config change in the window; only an unrelated notification-service email.batch_size change.
No errors in downstream dependencies; ledger-db only logged a deprecated TLS cipher warning.
api-gateway recorded 159 'upstream order-service returned 500 for POST /v1/orders' warnings from 12:13:07Z.

assumptions: marginProfile should be populated for FNO orders but is null in the new code path (either a code bug or a missing null-guard); no sample marginProfile payload was available to confirm the exact defect
No order-service config/flag change occurred outside the 2026-03-01..13:59 query window
Failure rate (~18%) reflects FNO share of order traffic; non-FNO orders are unaffected

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service to the pre-v2.14.0 version (or disable the new MarginCheckValidator / restore OrderRules.validateMargin()) to stop the 500s.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fault is in the code introduced by dep-5101 at 12:10Z; error rate has stayed ~18% since onset and no rollback has been done.

recommended_actions.action: Fix the null-dereference: null-guard marginProfile in MarginCheckValidator.validate (line 88) or ensure margin profiles are populated/loaded before validation for FNO orders.
recommended_actions.rationale: The NPE is at a fixed line for a specific order type, indicating a missing null check or unloaded profile.

recommended_actions.action: Add a canary/staged rollout with F&O order-path smoke tests in CI to catch validation regressions before full rollout.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 2-minute post-deploy regression reached ~18% error rate with no staged guardrail.

recommended_actions.action: Verify FNO margin-profile data population from ledger-db to confirm whether the new validator also needs a data-loading fix, not just a null guard.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes a pure code bug from a missing-data dependency; no marginProfile payload was observed in tooling.

A single deployment dep-5101 for order-service v2.14.0 occurred at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z by r.iyer with summary 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders' and changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain', 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()'. Status live, never rolled back.

findings.statement: The new code removed the legacy 'OrderRules.validateMargin()' and replaced it with MarginCheckValidator, whose line 88 dereferences a marginProfile that is null; this is a regression in the new validation path, not a downstream data outage (no dependency reports errors).

Historical incident HIST-109 is a bad_deployment regression (JWT library upgrade) resolved by rollback, corroborating that a release-introduced regression is the plausible class here; HIST-103/110/115 (dependency/infra/config) symptoms (504/timeouts/pool exhaustion) do not match the observed NPE.
